title: Lead Quantity Surveyor
description: Job Highlight This is a unique opportunity for a seasoned Lead Quantity Surveyor to significantly contribute to sustainable development initiatives across the Horn of Africa. The role offers the chance to apply expert knowledge in cost management and quantity surveying to high-impact infrastructure projects, work within a dynamic international environment, and advance a career with a leading UN organization dedicated to improving lives. Role Purpose The Lead Quantity Surveyor manages the comprehensive quantity surveying and cost management processes for civil engineering projects, providing authoritative advice and adapting established methodologies to ensure accurate cost estimation, procurement support, and financial control. This role is critical for the successful and efficient delivery of infrastructure initiatives, ensuring integrity, timeliness, and cost-effectiveness. Functions / Key Results Expected Site Assessment and Data Review Undertake complex/multi-site technical assessments and establish approaches/methodologies. Provide senior technical advice on the interpretation of drawings, surveys, specifications, geotechnical information, and other technical data to inform project design and cost decisions. Establish appropriate methodologies and approaches for quantity assessment, measurement, and cost estimation for complex infrastructure projects. Identify and proactively address technical, constructability, and cost risks, recommending mitigation measures and alternative solutions. Actively participate in multidisciplinary technical coordination and resolve complex technical issues. Engineering Estimates and Cost Planning and Analysis Lead and validate complex, high-value estimates and provide authoritative cost advice.. Provide authoritative technical advice to project management and senior stakeholders on quantities, cost estimates, technical specifications, pricing assumptions, and Bills of Quantities. Develop cost breakdowns using current market prices, labor rates, and material costs. Review and challenge estimates prepared by project teams or consultants, ensuring technical integrity, consistency, competitiveness, and value for money. Bills of Quantities (BoQ) Preparation Establish and promote standardized measurement methodologies, item descriptions, units, and quantity take-off approaches across projects. Ensure consistency and technical integrity between drawings, specifications, design changes, BoQs, and cost estimates. Provide technical leadership in resolving complex discrepancies between design documentation, specifications, quantities, and cost estimates. Develop guidance and quality-control mechanisms to improve the accuracy, consistency, and reliability of BoQs and quantity assessments. Procurement Support Provide authoritative technical advice to tender documents, including BoQs and specifications throughout procurement and bid evaluation . Advise on responses to bidder queries during the procurement process. Advise project and procurement stakeholders on cost competitiveness, technical compliance, risks, and value-for-money considerations. Review proposed contractual rates and commercial assumptions and advise on their technical and financial implications. Site Measurement and As-Built Quantification Advise on cost variation analysis, contractors’ claims analysis and new rate review during implementation, including advice on possible resolution Review and validate proposed new rates and cost adjustments, ensuring consistency with contractual provisions, market conditions, and established pricing methodologies. Provide senior technical recommendations on disputed quantities, variations, claims, and cost adjustments to support management decision-making. Lead the preparation and validation of as-built quantity assessments and ensure alignment with approved designs, site measurements, and contractor submissions. Provide technical advice supporting the certification and acceptance of completed work Documentation and Reporting Establish and oversee technical quality-control mechanisms for engineering estimates, BoQs, quantity measurements, cost data, and related documentation. Develop and maintain technical standards, procedures, guidance, templates, and tools for quantity surveying and engineering cost management. Establish and maintain reliable cost databases, benchmarks, historical pricing information, and lessons learned to support future infrastructure projects. Prepare high-level cost analysis and management reports, highlighting trends, risks, variances, and implications for project delivery. Provide senior management with advice and recommendations on project cost, commercial risks, and technical matters. Promote knowledge sharing and provide technical guidance and mentoring to project teams and less experienced personnel in engineering estimating, quantity surveying, measurement, and cost control. title: Bsc Midwifery
description: Company Description Chefe Health Center is a community-focused primary care facility serving diverse populations in Addis Ababa. The center provides essential maternal, neonatal, and child health services, along with general outpatient care and preventive health programs. Chefe Health Center emphasizes evidence-based practice, respectful and compassionate care, and collaboration among multidisciplinary teams. The facility is committed to improving health outcomes through accessible services, health education, and continuous quality improvement initiatives. Role Description The BSc Midwifery professional will provide comprehensive, person-centered care to pregnant individuals, birthing clients, newborns, and families in an on-site setting at Chefe Health Center in Addis Ababa. This full-time role includes conducting antenatal assessments, monitoring pregnancies, providing health education, and developing individualized care plans. The midwife will manage labor and delivery, perform safe births, monitor maternal and fetal wellbeing, and provide immediate newborn care, including essential resuscitation when needed. Daily duties also include postnatal follow-up, breastfeeding support, family planning counseling, and documentation of all care in line with clinical and regulatory standards. The role involves close collaboration with physicians, nurses, and other health professionals, participation in case discussions and referrals, and adherence to infection prevention, patient safety, and ethical guidelines. Qualifications Completed Bachelor of Science (BSc) in Midwifery from an accredited institution and valid professional registration or licensure, as required by local regulations. Clinical skills in antenatal, intrapartum, and postnatal care, including labor management, safe delivery techniques, newborn assessment, and emergency obstetric and neonatal care. Knowledge of maternal and child health guidelines, family planning, infection prevention and control, and standard treatment protocols relevant to primary healthcare settings. Strong communication and counseling abilities, including capacity to provide respectful, culturally sensitive care and clear health education to clients and families. Ability to maintain accurate documentation, use clinical records and reporting tools, and follow established policies, procedures, and quality assurance standards. Demonstrated teamwork and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary environment and participate in referrals and case management. Resilience and adaptability in busy clinical settings, including willingness to work shifts, respond to emergencies, and prioritize tasks safely and efficiently. Basic computer literacy and familiarity with electronic or paper-based health information systems; previous experience in a health center or hospital setting is an advantage.

title: Junior Site Engineer
description: Company Description Mugo Design and Build operates across key East African cities, including Addis Ababa, Nairobi, and Zanzibar, delivering design and construction services in diverse urban environments. The company is involved in projects that range from residential and commercial buildings to infrastructure developments. Team members collaborate closely across locations, gaining exposure to different regulatory frameworks, construction methods, and architectural styles. Joining Mugo Design and Build offers opportunities for professional growth, practical site experience, and participation in projects that shape the built environment. Role Description The Junior Site Engineer will support day-to-day site operations for construction projects in Addis Ababa. This full-time, on-site role involves assisting senior engineers in supervising works, coordinating with contractors and trades, monitoring progress against plans, and ensuring compliance with design specifications and safety standards. Responsibilities include conducting site inspections, supporting quality control activities, documenting site reports, and helping resolve technical issues as they arise. The Junior Site Engineer will also communicate regularly with project managers and design teams, helping to keep stakeholders informed of timelines, risks, and resource needs. Qualifications Candidates should possess strong on-site skills, including familiarity with construction processes and the ability to work safely and effectively at project locations. Candidates should possess solid communication skills, with the ability to collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, contractors, and stakeholders, and prepare clear site reports. Candidates should possess skills in quality control, including attention to detail, adherence to standards, and support for inspection and testing procedures. Candidates should possess foundational structural engineering knowledge, with an understanding of structural drawings, materials, and basic calculations. Candidates should possess civil engineering skills, preferably with a degree or diploma in Civil Engineering or a closely related field. Additional beneficial qualifications include familiarity with construction codes and regulations, basic proficiency in CAD or similar design tools, and strong organizational and time-management abilities. Ability to work on-site in Addis Ababa on a full-time basis and a willingness to learn from senior engineers and project leads.

title: Lead Structural Engineer
description: Job Highlight This is an exceptional opportunity for a seasoned Structural Engineer to lead the design and technical oversight of impactful infrastructure projects in the Horn of Africa. The role offers the chance to apply advanced engineering expertise to complex challenges, contribute to the region's development, and collaborate with diverse teams within a leading international organization, fostering professional growth and making a tangible difference in communities Role Purpose The Lead Structural Engineer manages and provides authoritative advice on structural design projects, adapting existing policies and approaches to meet emerging client and project needs within the Horn of Africa. The incumbent is responsible for independently performing structural analysis, developing design solutions, ensuring compliance with international standards, and supervising technical aspects of project delivery, thereby contributing to the successful implementation of UNOPS' infrastructure mandate. Functions / Key Results Expected Site Assessment and Site Investigation Follow-up Review site conditions including topography, terrain, and existing infrastructure to identify design constraints. Interpret topographic surveys, geotechnical reports, and relevant environmental data to support design decisions. Assess site-specific risks such as settlement, slope instability, and groundwater conditions. Evaluate soil properties and bearing capacity to inform foundation design. Support feasibility assessments and selection of appropriate structural systems. Structural Design Perform structural system selection, structural design and analysis of buildings and civil works, including superstructure and foundation systems under relevant load combinations. Develop structural solutions that are safe, durable, efficient, and constructible. Ensure appropriate consideration of load paths, stability, serviceability, and material performance. Apply relevant international and national design standards and codes. Design Deliverables Prepare structural drawings, design calculations, design reports, presentations, design brief, technical specifications, and Bills of Quantities (BoQs). Ensure completeness, accuracy, and compliance of all design outputs. Address design review comments and update deliverables accordingly. Maintain organized and traceable documentation of all design work. Procurement Support Provide technical input to tender document preparation, including specifications and BoQs. Support clarification of technical queries during the bidding process. Assist in the technical evaluation of proposals where required. Construction Support and Quality Assurance Respond to design clarification requests; Revise designs; Provide details when requested by the Project Implementation team Review shop drawings, method statements, and material submissions. Support resolution of technical issues encountered on site. Review as-built drawings and contribute to progress and quality reporting. Provide technical support during construction to ensure compliance with design intent and specifications. Coordination and Technical Interface Work closely with multidisciplinary teams including architectural, geotechnical, and MEP disciplines. Ensure proper integration of structural systems within the overall project design. Participate in technical discussions and coordination meetings as required. Knowledge Management Maintain proper documentation of structural design outputs and reports. Contribute to knowledge sharing and continuous improvement within the team. Education Requirements Required An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, or a related discipline, with a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience, is required. A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, or a related discipline, combined with a minimum of 7 years of relevant experience, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Required Experience Requirements Relevant professional experience in the structural design of buildings and civil works is required, including experience in the design and analysis of reinforced concrete and/or steel structures; preparation of structural drawings, design reports and Bills of Quantities (BoQs); use of structural design software such as ETABS, SAP2000, SAFE, Robot, or equivalent; and interpretation of topographic surveys and geotechnical investigation reports. A valid practicing professional Structural Engineering license is required (please attach to application). Desired Experience in infrastructure or public facility projects, international design standards, and/or working with the United Nations is desirable.

title: Project Assistant - SRHR Next Alliance Ethiopia
description: Amref Health Africa, founded in 1957, is the largest African-based international health development organisation. Headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, Amref implements programmes across 35 African countries , reaching more than 40 million people , with a strong operational presence in Africa and advocacy and fundraising offices in Europe and North America. Guided by its vision of lasting health change in Africa , Amref’s mission is to catalyse community-led, people-centred health systems and address the social determinants of health . Amref believes sustainable health transformation is driven from within communities and works to strengthen health systems while empowering communities to demand and access quality, affordable healthcare. Job Description Job Summary The Project Assistant will support day-to-day implementation of the SRH Next Alliance Project at field level, working closely with local government structures, health facilities, schools, youth and women-led groups, community actors, and project partners. The role will contribute to improving access to quality, youth-friendly, gender-responsive and disability-inclusive sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services and information, while strengthening community engagement, referral systems, accountability and local coordination. The Project Assistant will also support routine monitoring, documentation, reporting, activity logistics and follow-up of agreed actions across the assigned woredas. Frequent field travel is an essential part of the position. Project Context The Ethiopian SRH next Alliance, led by Plan Ethiopia and comprising five organizations, focuses on urgent SRH needs in Amhara, Tigray and Afar. The project prioritizes equitable, gender-responsive, disability-inclusive and youth-friendly services, local leadership, youth and women-led civil society organizations, stronger accountability, and coordinated action. Its three core outcome areas are: (1) increased availability, accessibility, acceptability and quality of SRH services; (2) increased access to and use of comprehensive, age-appropriate and disability-inclusive SRH information and education; and (3) a stronger enabling environment for the SRH of women, young people and marginalized groups. Roles And Responsibilities Project implementation and field coordination Support planning, organization and implementation of approved project activities in the assigned duty station and woredas, in line with workplans, budgets, technical guidance and Amref procedures. Maintain regular working relationships with woreda health offices, health facilities, schools, youth structures, women- and youth-led organizations, community leaders and other relevant stakeholders. Assist with coordination of meetings, trainings, dialogues, community events, outreach activities and review sessions, including participant mobilization, venue and material preparation, attendance documentation and action tracking. Conduct frequent field visits to assigned implementation sites and provide timely follow-up on agreed actions, implementation bottlenecks and emerging needs. Support conflict-sensitive and context-adaptive implementation, and promptly communicate access, operational or security concerns to the supervisor. Support to youth-friendly SRHR services and referral pathways Support health facilities and local stakeholders in the establishment, strengthening and routine follow-up of youth-friendly, confidential and integrated SRH service delivery arrangements, including youth-friendly service corners where applicable. Assist project teams to organize capacity-strengthening activities for SRH service providers on respectful, non-judgmental, adolescent- and gender-responsive, disability-inclusive and survivor-centred care. Support mobile and community outreach activities intended to reach remote, marginalized, out-of-school and conflict-affected adolescents and young people. Facilitate and follow up functional referral linkages among SRH, HIV/STI, SGBV response, psychosocial support, legal aid and other relevant services, in accordance with approved project approaches and safeguarding requirements. Support youth and community feedback mechanisms, service monitoring and other accountability activities aimed at identifying and addressing service gaps. SRH information, education and youth engagement Support peer education, structured youth dialogue, safe-space and youth club activities, including linkages between education activities and youth-friendly services. Assist schools and community structures in implementing approved age-appropriate SRH education activities, including relevant life-skills and menstrual health components. Support dissemination and use of approved SRH information through project channels, including digital and community-based approaches, while ensuring content is appropriate, inclusive and consistent with project guidance. Support risk mitigation by ensuring contracts receive appropriate review and documentation Act as a primary point of contact with procurement, academic departments, and administrative units regarding contract-related matters.
